title_en: Your family has a right to food grains from the ration shop
law: National Food Security Act, 2013, Sections 3, 8, 13, 14 and 15
rule_plain: If your family is a priority household, each person can get 5 kg of food grains a month at low prices from the ration system. Antyodaya Anna Yojana families can get 35 kg per family a month. If you do not get the grains you are owed, the State Government must pay you a food security allowance.
what_you_can_do: Complain through the State's grievance system, which may include call centres and help lines.
Complain to the District Grievance Redressal Officer of your district if you do not get your grains.
If you are not happy with that officer's order, you can appeal to the State Food Commission.
where_to_get_help: The District Grievance Redressal Officer of your district; the State Food Commission for appeals.
